newsitem.title: USA: Woman arrested in Wells Fargo case -FBI.
newsitem.headline: Woman arrested in Wells Fargo case -FBI.

text.p: The FBI said Tuesday it arrested a 27-year-old employee of Borg-Warner Security Corp's Wells Fargo unit over $2.5 million missing from the armoured services Youngstown, Ohio, office.
The $2.5 million, which disappeared Friday, has not been recovered, and an investigation by the FBI and Youngstown police continues, the FBI said in a statement.

Leesa Mazon of Struthers, Ohio, a Wells Fargo employee since October 1995, was charged with violating federal bank larceny statutes, Van Harp, special agent in charge of the FBI's Cleveland division, said in the FBI statement.

"Mazon is alleged to have been involved in the Nov. 29, 1996, disappearance of $2.5 million from the Wells Fargo office," Harp said. If convicted, she could face up to 10 years in federal prison, Harp said.
Mazon turned herself in to authorities in West Middlesex, Pa., Monday, and was being detained pending a preliminary hearing before a U.S. Magistrate, Harp said.
The FBI said the company offered a $50,000 reward for information leading to recovery of the funds. A Borg-Warner spokeswoman said it is co-operating but declined further comment.
